author: Fouled
body:
Map building FAQ

Hello everyone! I'm making this map building FAQ to guide and help others with map building and submitting maps. This will hopefully reduce some of the map making threads made by people.  Instead they can look on here for the help :)

How do you make a YML? 
You can learn how to make a YML by using  docs.avicus.net, you can also learn or look at some map YML's just to get an idea of how it looks like on, maps.avicus.net. 
If you are still having trouble, you may ask a mapdev or anybody that knows how to make a YML for help! :)

Where do I make a map?
You can make a map on single or on a server.

How do I make a map?
You can use mods/programs such as Worldedit, Voxelsniper, MCedit and more to help you! 
This would also help you complete maps faster, without placing every single block.

What are some world edit commands?
Some basic Worledit commands are:
- .//set (block)
- .//replace (block), (block)
- .//copy
- .//paste -a
- .//rotate (degrees)
- .//flip (direction)

Where do I get a walls template from?
You can either download a walls template from from: https://sites.google.com/site/mczonewiki/home/resources/templates/walls-template
Or you can make your own walls template. 
There are no certain dimensions. As you are allowed to make it any size you want aslong as it is comfortable for PVP and such (just don't make the area big or too small).

Can I make sequels to other peoples maps?
You need permission from the creator of the map. If you do not have permission, you may not create a sequel to other maps.

What is the maxium amount of monuments you can have per team?
6 monuments per team is the maximum.

Is it possible to have a 4 team DTM game?
Yes, it is possible to have a 4 team DTM match (example: Kings Fortress)

What is the process of maps?
Accept/Deny > Test the maps > Add them into rotations
If the map has good game-play and aesthetics and plays well overall, it will most likely pass the testing stage. 

How do you become a map developer?
Map developers are hand picked by how well they cooperate with others, YML skills, builds and work ethic.

What is the format in a map thread?
You can basically do any format you want, along as it has all the necessary requirements such as the download link and YML. I'll post my map format here, just to give an example.

(Map name) - (Gamemode)

Map name:
Creator: 
Contributors (optional):
Gamemode:
Download link:
YML:
Pictures:

How many creators are allowed?
There's not really a limit on how many creators there should be.
But around 3 creators would fit properly on the broadcast. If you add the rest of the people under the section contributor in the YML. 
If there was more creators added, it would be really squished.

How do I get a void world? 
You can download a void world here: http://www.mediafire.com/download/kczs5s9qu0u4e34/Empty+World.zip


Note:
I will be updating this thread frequently, when there's more questions asked (or if I can think of anymore xP)

replies.author: Matic0B
replies.body:
I will be adding onto this a little bit.

Void World

You can create a void world in single player by using the flat world and removing all layers so you are only left with air / void. Then you can use single player commands that are implemented in Minecraft to spawn a block and then you can start building though this is not the easiest way.

My recommendation would be creating you own Bukkit server that you would host on your computer (local host server). If you have a lower end PC it might not be that great for you but if you can run a server for yourself, this will be really useful.
When it comes to the plugins you should install Multiverse and WorldEdit. Depending on your needs you might want other stuff like Itemizer as well. Then you would download a custom void generator for Multiverse (I used CleanRoomGenerator).
After you get your server set and running connect to it. The best way would be just leaving the IP blank in properties so you can connect via localhost. Then create a world with /mvcreate and use the void generator (in my case -g CleanRoomGenerator:.). TP to that world and you will have a void world forever where you can build. Create the first block with using WorldEdit.

WorldEdit commands

Some more useful commands are these:
  • //pos1 (sets the first position. really useful if you don't have a block to select a region from midair)
  • //pos2 (sets the second position. same as above)
  • //cyl (creates a cylinder. //hcyl is a hollow cylinder. you need to include values for block type and size)
  • //sphere (creates a sphere. //hsphere is a hollow sphere. you need to include values for block type and size)
A bit more of an advanced command is //brush but it is really useful when creating maps. From using it to create spheres that you can use for terraforming to smoothing terrain to make it looks better if you are attempting to use it for landscape.

I would also like to say something about the system of accepting maps.

I think that before accepting/denying a map you guys should test it. In the OP you say that you accept/deny and then test which IMO is wrong. Even if a map is not the best at aesthetics it can have amazing gameplay so you should first test it. If it plays well and looks good then add it. If it plays well but has aeshtetic flaws try to work on them with the map creators. That would be better but thats just my opinion.

replies.author: resepignev
replies.body:
Sadly it's not working. Several ppl tried to do it, but the mapdevs are saying it doesn't work. Here are some examples/cases:

(A) 1 Monument in the Center:
- Every Team would have the same coordinates for the obsidian in the middle. The problem is you can't break your own monument.

(B) 2 Monuments for each team: 
- So in total 8 Monuments (2 for 4 teams) That would mean every team has to destroy 6 Monuments to win (6*4=24). But there are only 8 of them. That's why it doesn't work.

(C) The plugin:
- The Nebula plugin doesn't support it. The creator of that plugin never thought about the case a Map Creator wants 4 Teams in a DTM or only 1 Monument at all.

replies.author: badgg
replies.body:
Sorry for the late response, but if you wish to add certain amount of ores without doing it manually... 
Selecting the region with WorldEdit.
//replace stone 20%diamondore,20%ironore,20%coalore,40%stone
Essentially, that replaces stone with 20 percent iron, coal and diamond ore... alongside the 40 percent of stone. 

It is up to you how frequent an ore appears, but this method is probably the best for beginners.

replies.author: jracer15
replies.body: When it comes to pasting walls quads I'm spending hours using //rotate //flip and the other commands.  What exact steps to paste the quads correctly? (World Edit of course, I tried McEdit and it took me on an acid trip.)
replies.body_tagged: When it comes to pasting walls quads I'm spending hours using //rotate //flip and the other commands.  What exact steps to paste the quads correctly? (World Edit of course, I tried McEdit and it took me on an acid trip.)

replies.author: steven5703
replies.body:
1. Select the entire quad, make sure its a PERFECT square or it will mess up the alignment
  2. Stand in the very center (must be the EXACT center of the map) of the walls map (not the quad, the walls map)
  3. Type //copy
  4. Type //rotate 90
  5. Type //paste
  6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 until all quads are filled

  2. Stand in the very center (must be the EXACT center of the map) of the walls map (not the quad, the walls map)

  4. Type //rotate 90
  5. Type //paste
  6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 until all quads are filled

replies.author: Pavlo
replies.body: When you //copy a region, remember where within it you are standing. For example if you select a tower, stand on the very tip of it when you type //copy. I hope this made sense! x)
